resource_envelope.headline: The design fits only inside a 363-551ms SOAP-latency band. Its own assumed 500ms sits inside that band, but the lower edge is BELOW the assumption and the upper edge is only 10% above it - an unsafe margin for a parameter nobody has measured. Outside the band jobs do not defer, they expire against retryUntil and MASS-FAIL via markJobAsFailedIfAlreadyExceedsMaxAttempts().
resource_envelope.cold_start: 305,228 jobs over a 1,440-min spread needs 106 jobs/min. 250ms OK; 500ms OK at 2,618 min (only 9.1% margin vs the 2,880-min deadline); 1000ms FAILS (5,156 min, +79%); 2000ms FAILS (+256%).
resource_envelope.steady_state: 76,307/day is the ARRIVAL rate; real call volume is 76,307-228,921/day because an unresolvable row is called 3x. Fits at 250ms; at 500ms only if the branch match rate >= 0.30.
not_the_problem: GIN write amplification: +37-48% relative but <=0.062ms absolute, 4.7s/day fleet-wide - reviewers right on mechanism, wrong on magnitude
resource_envelope.confirmed_review_finding: The status IN-list SAOP does force a Sort of the whole window (57,513 index entries -> Sort 47,928 rows) instead of index-ordered early termination. Isolated by control: status=1 plans as Parallel Index Scan Backward with NO Sort, terminating after ~1,590 rows. Cost is small, but the mechanism claim was correct.
levers: HORIZON_SUPERVISOR_2_PROCESSES is a pure linear multiplier needing NO code change: 2 processes moves the binding threshold 363ms -> 741ms

resource_envelope.verdict_revised: Originally FAIL. REVISED to PASS once the ticket owner confirmed HORIZON_SUPERVISOR_2_PROCESSES=2 in production (the repo default is 1, which is what the measurement assumed). Throughput scales linearly, so concurrency 2 doubles every measured figure.
resource_envelope.concurrency_production: 2 per host (owner-confirmed). Host count is NOT knowable from the repo - config/deploy.yml builds web_hosts from a deploy-time env var - so 2 is the FLOOR; every additional web host runs its own Horizon workers container against the same Redis queue and multiplies throughput again.

resource_envelope.new_live_defect: retry_after=90 (config/queue.php) vs GetOrgHotlistCaseInfo::$timeout=600. Masked at concurrency 1; LIVE at 2. A job past 90s is released while still running, so a second worker duplicates the SOAP call and double-increments branch_lookup_attempts - which at ceiling 3 can seal a row prematurely. Contradicts okf/concepts/jobs-and-queues.md ('never let a job exceed the worker timeout'). Driver had deferred this explicitly on a single-process assumption that was wrong.

round_7_consensus_findings: ALL 3 LANES - No RDN eligibility predicate: candidates() filters org+status+created_at only. No integration_id=RDN and no rdn_api_key/hasRdnAccount gate. remote_order_id is unique only per (org,integration) - a unique index proves the id spaces overlap - so a mixed-integration org can have RDN's answer for a DIFFERENT order written as its branch (data corruption). Also burns ~90% of the fleet budget on orgs/rows that can never resolve, and INSERTs synthetic hotlist_json rows that CDC downstream.

ALL 3 LANES - The flat 24/org/run cap makes the feature ineffective for the orgs it exists for. Coverage = cap/arrival-rate: largest org 24 of ~12,385/day = 0.19%. Even the MEAN org (~27.7/day) is above the cap. Rows not selected age out of the 7-day window permanently. Flat allocation across orgs spanning 3 orders of magnitude of volume is the error - the fleet budget (83,832/day) is actually close to fleet arrivals (~96,850/day), so PROPORTIONAL allocation would nearly keep up.

ALL 3 LANES - DRIVER ERROR: gatedByQueue() on RdnJob removes the only PER-CALL throttle from four paginated sibling jobs. The driver's premise was false: RateLimited keys on md5(limiterName.key), NOT the raw 'rdn-api:{org}', so the two layers never shared a bucket - middleware charges per JOB, service layer charged per CALL. GetOrgBranchZips makes one SOAP call PER BRANCH, now charged as 1.

ALL 3 LANES - {low} is one process per host and already carries transactional mail (invites, billing receipts, Scout end-of-shift) plus the at-most-once hourly RDN metrics push. Adding 83,832 jobs/day - permanently, not a backfill - head-of-line blocks all of it by hours. The 120/min drain is UNMEASURED and retryUntil derives from the same number, so it cannot detect its own shortfall.

LANE 3 - DRIVER ERROR: orderBy('created_at') ASC defeats forward-only attribution. Enrichment lands at age ~7 days, AFTER the ->Open transition already appended with branch_id=0, so Total Assignments stays 0 while Repossessions (weeks later) attributes - producing exactly the contradictory Assignments-0 / Repossessions-N / Rate-0% screen. The ORIGINAL orderByDesc was correct for this design; the driver's F9 FIFO change caused it.

LANES 1+2 - Transport failures (SOAP fault, TLS/DNS, rotated key) are indistinguishable from 'RDN has no branch' and burn the 3-attempt give-up counter. A 3-day RDN outage permanently seals every in-window row with no un-seal path, no reset command, no TTL.

LANE 2 - recordUnresolvedLookup() unconditionally nulls branch_id, so a resolve-then-miss race loses a resolved branch. Also ::int on the write path vs ::numeric on the read path: a fractional counter passes the read guard and throws on write, re-taking the FIFO front forever.

round_11_blocking_finding.claim: The Assignments/Accepted cohort can NEVER be branch-attributed under this design.
round_11_blocking_finding.mechanism: public.log_status_changes is an AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on public.hotlist. On INSERT, OLD is null so COALESCE(OLD.status,0)=0, and a hotlist inserted at status=Open(1) writes a (0->1) hotlist_status_log row AT INSERT TIME. That row is exactly HotlistStatusAggregate::scopeAccepted (new_status=Open AND old_status IN (Other=0, NewFromClient=90)) and is counted by scopeOpenAssignments (new_status=Open, any old_status). clarity.hotlist_status_aggregate is append-only with branch_id in the sorting key and is permanently off-limits, so a row appended with branch_id=0 stays 0 forever. Enrichment lands 24-48h later (daily schedule + up to 1440min child spread), so it can never precede the transition.
round_11_blocking_finding.measured_magnitude: Production, 14 days, transitions to Open: old_status=0 (INSERT-synthesised) 2,455,313 = 91.87%; old_status=90 (real NewFromClient->Open) 35,142 = 1.31%. So ~92% of the cohort is unattributable by construction.
round_11_blocking_finding.consequence: Branch-filtered TotalAssignmentsWidget, TotalAcceptedWidget and ClientRankedMetricsBatch assignments/accepted are permanently ~0, while TotalRepossessionsWidget (new_status=3, days later) attributes normally -> AverageRecoveryRateWidget renders 0%. That is the contradictory Assignments-0 / Repossessions-N / Rate-0% screen the ticket exists to fix, reproduced BY the fix.
round_11_blocking_finding.why_it_was_missed: Agent QA seeded ClickHouse rows with branch_id ALREADY SET - it validated the end state, not the pipeline. It therefore proved 'the filter works if branch_id is populated' and never exercised enrichment latency vs INSERT-time transition. Driver scoped that QA.

round_11_other_consensus: BOTH lanes 1+2: the per-org crc32 phase is applied as a rotation of the whole series, so index 0 (the NEWEST row) gets delay = phase, mean ~12h and up to 20.8h measured. This defeats the newest-first property established specifically to beat the transition. Tests cannot see it: dispatchedDelays() SORTS the offsets and discards the hotlist<->slot mapping.

BOTH lanes 1+2: no re-run/cross-run dedup. Re-running app:rdn (the documented canary check) re-selects the identical set with deterministic phases, so duplicates land in the SAME slot -> 2 SOAP calls and branch_lookup_attempts 0->2 for one answer, burning 2 of 3 attempts.
ALL THREE lanes: app:rdn --force with NO org argument forces the entire fleet past the kill switch, contradicting the canary docblock.

lane 2 M3 / lane 3 L1: GetOrgHotlistCases has an unguarded each() loop with tries=1 and no retryUntil, so one mid-run failure loses the org's day AND emits no summary line - which the runbook (driver-written) tells the operator means the kill switch stopped it. The runbook mis-diagnoses the most likely failure.
lane 2 M5: retryUntil converts benign supersession into permanent failed_jobs rows, and nothing prunes failed_jobs (no queue:prune-failed anywhere in routes/).
lane 3 M5: Branch::where(org_id)->where(branch_name)->first() has no ORDER BY and branch_name is not unique -> nondeterministic attribution into an append-only aggregate.

lane 3 M6: for orgs above the 1000/run cap, newest-first means yesterday's misses never get a 2nd attempt - coverage collapses to cap/arrivals (~10% for the largest org), and the seal never fires so it cannot free budget.

lane 3 M7: ClientTableBranchFilterTest still only pins type coercion. prep-context named a consumer-level test as a deliverable and as the blind spot that let this ship for ~10 months. Not delivered - which is why nothing in the change would have caught H1.

residuals_for_followup: RdnJob carries $timeout=600 vs retry_after=90, so GetOrgBranches/GetOrgRdnClients/GetOrgAgents/GetOrgBranchZips have the same duplicate-execution window at concurrency>1. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here. Cannot take the same fix: those jobs paginate (one job = many SOAP calls) so they cannot be bounded under 90s without a redesign (batching, or a connection with a longer reservation). Needs its own ticket.
The per-org cap of 1000 silently truncates high-volume orgs with no log/metric (the run summary reports `capped` but nothing alerts).
rdn-case-info and rdn-api are two uncoordinated per-org budgets against one RDN account, so an opted-in org can reach 2x its vendor limit.
